newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian markets active on foreign interest.
newsitem.headline: Romanian markets active on foreign interest.

text.p: Romanian financial markets reached new heights on Thursday, boosted by growing interest from foreign investors attracted by a newly stable leu currency and promises of market incentives.
Foreign money has poured into the markets in recent days, pushing equity turnover to a record high and boosting foreign exchange volume and trade in government paper.
Foreign investors have begun entering Romanian markets due to evidence of a firmer commitment to reforms from the centrist coalition government.
The government last November ended seven years of leftist administration after the fall of communism.

The bourse rallied throughout the week and hit a turnover record of 25.73 billion lei ($3.7 million) on Thursday thanks to heavy first-tier trading and a special deal in high-cap Azomures fertiliser maker. The previous record, set in mid-February, was 6.7 billion lei.
Traders said foreign interest was behind the Azomures deal.

The leu has regained a measure of stability over the past four weeks, trading near 7,100 to the dollar. It gained support from repatriation of export earnings and from hard currency flows following a rising interest in Romanian equities and government securities promising high returns.

Central bank data on Thursday showed a record foreign exchange market volume of $139.6 million for the previous day, when interbank trading amounted to $62.49 million. That was considerably higher than the March daily average of $22.7 million on interbank trading of $7 million.

The budding over-the-counter (OTC) market has also been in focus, hitting a turnover record of 40.3 billion lei in the first four of this week's five sessions. The OTC market had average weekly turnover of 16.8 billion lei in March.
The government has speeded up its legislative agenda on reform to draw in more foreign investment.

Laws on foreign ownership of land and bank privatisation were approved in the past week and the government promised to rush through legislation on portfolio investors. Traders said the law was expected to set a very low tax on repatriating capital gains.
The central bank took steps to boost the primary and secondary markets for state treasury bills.
Central bank rules set no clear norms on foreign access to the market, but traders said investors abroad were still keen to enter direct T-bills trading.

Foreign investors are now entitled to buy government securities as clients of commercial banks operating in Romania. All T-bills issues in the primary market -- offering yields of up to 232 percent annually -- have been heavily oversubscribed. ($ = 7010 Romanian Lei)
